definition: A functional programming language built around lightweight processes and message passing.
example: A message server isolates each client connection in its own process.

definition: A human language used for spoken and written communication.
example: An archivist transcribes an Ewondo interview.

definition: A programming language for specifying and verifying properties of programs with dependent types.
example: A developer proves that a lookup function stays within array bounds.

definition: A functional-first, statically typed programming language on .NET.
example: An analyst maps a typed function over a list of sensor readings.

sense_note: Confirm the intended language identifier because Fali can name different languages.

definition: An object-oriented programming language designed for portability across runtime platforms.
example: A developer uses Fantom collections to organize configuration records.

definition: A standardized language based primarily on Tagalog.
example: A translator prepares Filipino subtitles for a public information video.

definition: A human language used for written and spoken communication.
example: An editor proofreads a Finnish museum guide.

definition: A stack-oriented programming language in which words operate on values placed on a stack.
example: A developer defines a word that adds the top two stack values.

definition: A compiled language widely used for numerical and scientific computing.
example: A scientist uses Fortran to update a matrix in a simulation.

definition: A human language used in writing and speech across multiple regional varieties.
example: A translator checks a French instruction manual.

definition: A label covering a group of closely related languages.
example: An editor asks whether a Frisian translation should use West Frisian.

definition: A human language with multiple varieties and writing conventions.
example: A radio producer verifies which Fula variety to use for a local broadcast.

definition: A human language used in spoken and written communication.
example: A recorder captures an oral account in Galo.

definition: A BASIC-derived language and development environment for building applications.
example: A developer builds a desktop form with a click handler.

definition: A human language used in oral and written communication.
example: A teacher records a Garifuna dialogue for language practice.

definition: A human language used in written and spoken communication across several standard varieties.
example: An editor checks a German software guide.

definition: A structured notation for describing software behavior with scenarios and steps.
example: A test writer specifies an expected result using Given, When, and Then.

definition: A human language used in speech and writing.
example: A translator checks a Gikuyu community announcement.

definition: A compiled programming language with built-in concurrency primitives and garbage collection.
example: A developer sends work items to a worker goroutine through a channel.

definition: A query language and execution specification for requesting typed API data.
example: A client requests a product's name without requesting other available fields.

definition: A human language label covering modern usage and historical forms written with the Greek alphabet.
example: An editor checks a Modern Greek product description.
sense_note: Specify the historical stage if relevant.

definition: A JVM programming language with scripting features and Java interoperability.
example: A build engineer writes a Gradle task in Groovy.

definition: A human language written using the Gujarati script.
example: A reviewer checks a Gujarati enrollment form.

definition: A statically checked programming language derived from PHP and used with HHVM.
example: A developer adds type annotations to a collection-processing function.

definition: A human language used in speech and writing, distinct from French.
example: An interpreter explains a hospital appointment in Haitian Creole.

definition: A formal language for describing hardware structure or behavior for simulation and sometimes synthesis.
example: An engineer describes the behavior of a clocked register for simulation.

definition: A statically typed, purely functional programming language with non-strict evaluation.
example: A developer pattern-matches an optional value before displaying a result.

definition: A human language used in speech, writing, and broadcasting.
example: A broadcaster reads a Hausa news bulletin.

definition: A named variety of Kannada.
example: A linguist compares a recorded Havyaka Kannada expression with a standard Kannada form.

definition: A human language used for speaking, writing, and teaching.
example: A teacher records Hawaiian pronunciations for a beginner lesson.

definition: A statically typed programming language that can compile to several target platforms or languages.
example: A game developer shares a Haxe gameplay module between builds.

definition: A human language used in spoken and written communication.
example: A researcher transcribes a Haya oral history.

definition: A human language written in the Hebrew alphabet, with historical and modern forms.
example: An editor reviews the labels in a Modern Hebrew interface.

definition: A human language whose standard written form uses Devanagari.
example: A translator checks a Hindi transit announcement.

definition: A broad language label covering multiple varieties relevant to speech and translation.
example: An interpreter checks which Hmong variety a caller prefers.
sense_note: Specify the variety where exact language matching matters.

definition: A label for related varieties of Southern Min used in spoken and written communication.
example: A localization team confirms the target Hokkien variety for narration.

definition: A human language used in spoken and written communication.
example: A language teacher reviews a Hopi pronunciation exercise.

definition: A markup language that gives web documents structure and meaning.
example: A developer marks the main page title with a heading element.
